html:
The annexation of Crimea was Russia's seizure of the Crimean peninsula from Ukraine in February and March 2014, after the Euromaidan revolution in Kyiv.

Soldiers without insignia, later admitted to be Russian troops, took the Crimean parliament and key sites from 27 February. A referendum held on 16 March under occupation, and not recognised by most countries, was said to show huge support for joining Russia. Russia annexed Crimea on 18 March. The United Nations General Assembly called the vote invalid, and Western countries imposed sanctions. In April Russia-backed separatists rose in Donbas, beginning a war that grew into the full invasion of 2022. Crimean Tatars, deported by Stalin in 1944, again faced repression.
sum: The annexation of Crimea was Russia's seizure of the Crimean peninsula from Ukraine in February and March 2014, after the Euromaidan revolution in Kyiv.
